newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks pulled down by brewing, tobacco.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks pulled down by brewing, tobacco.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended down for the fourth straight day, pulled down by brewing and cigarettes.
Bogota's IBB index fell 0.95 percent to 1,198.37 amid a 6.2 billion peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index dipped 0.84 percent to 18,200.74 amid a 5.6 billion peso volume.

"There are interested buyers, including foreign funds, but exiting shareholders are carrying out pocket-to-pocket cross deals because they want to rearrange their portfolios or don't believe prices will rise much more," one Medellin broker said.
One of the day's biggest fallers was brewing giant Bavaria, down 1.69 percent to 7,813 in Bogota and down 1.84 percent to 7,803 in Medellin.

The falls were partly due to profit-taking and partly a response to Bavaria's failure to call a shareholders meeting, as announced in March, to propose a share split along the lines of the company's industrial and investment operations.

Most of the other falls were in shares of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate. Cigarette manufacturer Coltabaco was unchanged at 3,900 in Bogota but fell 2.56 percent to 3,800 on profit-taking in Medellin.
